## How it works

Since `push_sessions` gates pushing the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch as a whole, the way to get `transcript.jsonl` pushed is to include it in the checkpoint tree: when `strategy_options.push_compact_transcripts` is `true`, every checkpoint write stores a condensed `transcript.jsonl` (generated by `transcript/compact` from the already-redacted `full.jsonl` content) next to `full.jsonl` in the session subdirectory. It then rides along on every push of the checkpoints branch. Default is `false` — nothing changes unless the option is explicitly set to `true`.

## Changes

- **`settings/settings.go`** — `IsPushCompactTranscriptsEnabled()` method plus a context-loading package-level variant, following the existing `IsFilteredFetchesEnabled`/`IsSignCheckpointCommitsEnabled` patterns. Only an explicit boolean `true` enables it.
- **`checkpoint/committed.go`** — `writeTranscript` now calls `writeCompactTranscript` when the setting is on. It runs after the Codex sanitization step so the compact converter sees the same bytes as `full.jsonl`. Generation is **best-effort**: a conversion or blob failure logs a warning and never blocks the checkpoint write, since hooks have no retry path.
- **`paths/paths.go`** — new `CompactTranscriptFileName = "transcript.jsonl"` constant.
- **`agent/registry.go`** — new `NameForAgentType()` helper with a static display-type → registry-slug map (e.g. "Claude Code" → "claude-code"), falling back to the live registry for external agents. The compact format's `agent` field wants the slug, and a static map keeps it deterministic regardless of which agent packages are linked in.
- **Docs** — updated the checkpoint layout diagrams in `committed.go`, `checkpoint.go`, and `docs/architecture/sessions-and-checkpoints.md` with the new optional file and a paragraph explaining the option.

## Tests

- `TestIsPushCompactTranscriptsEnabled` (settings): missing / true / false / wrong-type cases.
- `TestWriteCommitted_CompactTranscript` (checkpoint): with the option enabled, `transcript.jsonl` lands in the session tree with the compact format (`"agent":"claude-code"`); disabled by default, only `full.jsonl` is written.

Two design notes worth knowing: the compact transcript covers the full session (same scope as `full.jsonl`, no `StartLine` truncation), and it's written as a single blob — no chunking, since compact output is much smaller than the full transcript. Also, because each session write clears its subdirectory first, turning the option off stops including the file on the next checkpoint write.
